## Results

We screened public human RNA-seq libraries for papillomavirus reads under three discovery strategies (Methods): an unbiased prevalence sweep of skin and related tissues (`r comma(stats$n_screened)` libraries screened), a targeted query of productive cutaneous lesions providing positive controls (`r stats$n_targeted` wart/epidermodysplasia-verruciformis skin libraries), and a broadened skin-neoplasia sweep capturing cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), actinic keratosis (AK) and Bowen disease (`r comma(stats$n_csc)` libraries screened). Throughout, every screened library, including HPV-negative ones, was scored as papillomavirus reads per million (RPM) so that infection burden could be separated from sequencing depth, and each sample was annotated as primary tissue, cell line, or engineered material.

### HPV signal in public RNA-seq is dominated by cell-line and engineered artefacts

In the unbiased sweep, HPV positivity was strongly concentrated in non-primary material. Engineered libraries were HPV-positive in `r f2(stats$eng_pct)`% of cases (95% CI `r pci(stats$eng_lo, stats$eng_hi)`) and cell-line libraries in `r f2(stats$cl_pct)`% (`r pci(stats$cl_lo, stats$cl_hi)`), versus only `r f2(stats$clin_pct)`% (`r pci(stats$clin_lo, stats$clin_hi)`) of clinical primary-tissue libraries (@tbl-positivity). In logistic regression this corresponded to roughly five-fold higher odds of positivity for engineered (OR `r fo(stats$eng_or)`, 95% CI `r oci(stats$eng_or_lo, stats$eng_or_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$eng_or_p)`) and cell-line (OR `r fo(stats$cl_or)`, `r oci(stats$cl_or_lo, stats$cl_or_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$cl_or_p)`) samples relative to clinical tissue (likelihood-ratio *P* = `r fp(stats$lr_p)`). These positives were almost entirely the high-risk mucosal alpha types: HPV18 accounted for `r stats$hpv18_cl`/`r stats$hpv18_tot` of its calls in cell lines and HPV16 for `r stats$hpv16_cl`/`r stats$hpv16_tot` (@supptbl-types), the expected signature of integrated-HPV cell lines such as HeLa and of their well-documented cross-contamination of archived sequencing data. Genuine primary skin therefore carries HPV at a low rate (2–4%, below), and the apparent abundance of HPV in public transcriptomes is largely a laboratory artefact that must be partitioned out before any prevalence claim.

### Skin neoplasia carries only trace HPV, not productive infection, and this is not a depth artefact

The central question, whether HPV is transcriptionally active in cSCC/AK or present only as a hit-and-run footprint, was resolved by the depth-normalised burden analysis (@fig-rpm). Productive controls (warts/condyloma) were detected at or above the control-calibrated detection floor (`r p1(stats$floor_rpm)` RPM) in `r pp(stats$ctrl_pctfloor)`% of libraries, with a median burden of `r comma(stats$ctrl_medrpm)` RPM; the EV biopsy tier, sequenced most deeply of all (median `r mreads(stats$ev_medreads)` reads), reached it in `r pp(stats$ev_pctfloor)`% (median `r p1(stats$ev_medrpm)` RPM). In stark contrast, the neoplasia tier reached this floor in only `r pp(stats$neo_pctfloor)`% of libraries (median `r formatC(stats$neo_medrpm, format="f", digits=3)` RPM), six orders of magnitude below the productive controls, despite being sequenced almost four times more deeply than they were (median `r mreads(stats$neo_medreads)` vs `r mreads(stats$ctrl_medreads)` reads). Unselected skin, once the peri-lesional and EV material that the targeted queries had swept into it was reassigned to its own tiers (Methods), forms an almost clean null: `r pp(stats$uns_pctfloor)`% of `r comma(stats$uns_n)` libraries reach the floor.

![Depth-normalised HPV transcript burden distinguishes productive warts, EV and peri-lesional mucosa from a trace-level signal in skin neoplasia and unselected skin. Each point is one Kraken2-screened RNA-seq library, scored as papillomavirus reads per million (RPM: Papillomaviridae clade reads ÷ (unclassified + root reads) × 10⁶) and grouped by population tier: unselected skin (*n* = `r comma(stats$uns_n)`), cell lines (`r comma(stats$cl2_n)`), productive controls (warts/condyloma; `r stats$ctrl_n`), epidermodysplasia verruciformis biopsies (EV; `r stats$ev_n`), cutaneous neoplasia (cSCC/actinic keratosis; `r stats$neo_n`), peri-lesional mucosa (condyloma-adjacent tissue; `r stats$per_n`), and other tissues (`r comma(stats$oth_n)`). Points are jittered horizontally; boxes show the median and interquartile range; the *y*-axis is log~10~-scaled (RPM + 0.05). The dashed red line marks the control-calibrated detection floor (`r p1(stats$floor_rpm)` RPM, the 5th percentile of productive-control libraries). Productive controls lie far above the floor (median `r comma(stats$ctrl_medrpm)` RPM; `r pp(stats$ctrl_pctfloor)`% of libraries above floor), as do EV biopsies (`r pp(stats$ev_pctfloor)`%) and peri-lesional mucosa (`r pp(stats$per_pctfloor)`%), whereas neoplasia and unselected skin sit near zero (`r pp(stats$neo_pctfloor)`% and `r pp(stats$uns_pctfloor)`% above floor) despite neoplasia being sequenced far more deeply than the productive controls (median `r mreads(stats$neo_medreads)` vs `r mreads(stats$ctrl_medreads)` reads). Tier assignment is by metadata precedence with curated corrections (Methods): EV *cultures* (immortalised keratinocyte EV models) remain in the cell-line tier, whereas the EV tier holds the `r stats$ev_n` EV patient skin biopsies.](figure1.png){#fig-rpm}

This gap is not explained by sequencing depth. Modelling productive-level detection (RPM ≥ floor) as a function of population tier and log sequencing depth, productive controls exceeded unselected skin by close to four orders of magnitude (Fisher exact OR `r fo(stats$fish_or)`, 95% CI `r fo(stats$fish_lo)` to `r fo(stats$fish_hi)` under separation, *P* = `r fp(stats$fish_p)`), while neoplasia sat an order of magnitude above skin (OR `r fo(stats$m2b_or)`, 95% CI `r oci(stats$m2b_lo, stats$m2b_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2b_p)`). That contrast is easier to read on the absolute scale from which the odds ratios derive: `r stats$ctrl_pos_floor`/`r stats$ctrl_n` productive controls cross the floor, against `r stats$neo_pos_floor`/`r comma(stats$neo_n)` neoplasia libraries and `r stats$uns_pos_floor`/`r comma(stats$uns_n)` skin libraries. Neoplasia is thus measurably, but marginally, above a near-zero baseline, and remains roughly `r round(stats$ctrl_pctfloor/stats$neo_pctfloor)`-fold below the productive controls in detection rate.

Crucially, that marginal excess is not productive burden, and it is not bought by depth. Sequencing depth raised the odds of detecting *any* HPV read (OR per log₁₀ reads `r fo(stats$m2a_l10_or)`, `r oci(stats$m2a_l10_lo, stats$m2a_l10_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2a_l10_p)`), but it did not raise the odds of reaching the detection floor, either as a covariate across tiers (OR `r fo(stats$m2b_l10_or)`, `r oci(stats$m2b_l10_lo, stats$m2b_l10_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2b_l10_p)`) or within the neoplasia tier alone (OR `r fo(stats$neo_depth_or)`, 95% CI `r oci(stats$neo_depth_lo, stats$neo_depth_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$neo_depth_p)`). The deepest cSCC/AK libraries, at `r p1(stats$neo_maxreads)`M reads, did not cross the productive floor. Consistent with a residual hit-and-run footprint rather than active infection, neoplasia showed a clear excess of *trace* HPV (any read; OR `r fo(stats$m2a_or)`, 95% CI `r oci(stats$m2a_lo, stats$m2a_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2a_p)` vs unselected skin) alongside its small floor-level excess, but neither amounted to productive burden. The depth-matched detection profile confirms the same pattern non-parametrically: across every sequencing-depth bin, productive controls detect at 90–100% while neoplasia and unselected skin stay near zero (@suppfig-depth). At population scale, then, HPV in cutaneous neoplasia is a low-level, transcriptionally inactive trace, the signature predicted by the hit-and-run model, and not the productive infection seen in warts.

Most of the small floor-level excess is in fact attributable to a handful of libraries the broadened SCC/CIN query captured: `r stats$cin_n` of the `r stats$neo_pos_floor` above-floor neoplasia libraries are high-risk *mucosal* HPV16 cases (CIN/SCC), conservatively retained in the neoplasia tier (@supptbl-cin). Excluding them halves the effect, lowering cutaneous-neoplasia floor-level detection to `r pp(stats$neo_pctfloor_cut)`% (OR vs skin `r fo(stats$m2b_or_cut)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2b_p_cut)`) and strengthening the productivity contrast against warts/EV (OR `r fo(stats$m3_or_cut)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m3_p_cut)`), so the retained tier is the conservative choice.

### The assay detects bona fide productive cutaneous HPV, including genuine infections in primary skin

That the trace neoplasia signal reflects biology rather than assay insensitivity is established by the positive controls, which the pipeline detects robustly. Among targeted wart/EV libraries, `r round(stats$m3_ctrl_pct)`% (`r stats$m3_ctrl_prod`/`r stats$m3_ctrl_n`) met the strict productive criterion (≥3 L1 major-capsid reads), spanning the classic cutaneous repertoire: wart-associated alpha types (HPV2, HPV27, HPV57), low-risk mucocutaneous types (HPV6, HPV11), and beta/gamma types (@supptbl-types). Productive infection was significantly more frequent in these controls than among HPV-positive neoplasia libraries (`r round(stats$m3_neo_pct)`%, `r stats$m3_neo_prod`/`r stats$m3_neo_n`; Fisher exact OR `r fo(stats$m3_or)`, 95% CI `r oci(stats$m3_lo, stats$m3_hi)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m3_p)`).

Even so, a minority of genuine, non-cell-line skin lesions did harbour unambiguous productive infection, showing that the trace-level population result does not exclude real cutaneous HPV disease. The strongest cases were a cSCC/CIN skin library productively infected with the gamma-type HPV12 (99.8% genome coverage; L1 = 1,803, L2 = 3,546 reads), two HPV16-productive cSCC libraries, and two "other-tissue" libraries (an actinic keratosis and a carcinoma) co-infected with the gamma types HPV96 and HPV182 at near-complete genome coverage (98–99%) and high depth (60–245×), with hundreds of L1 and L2 reads each (@supptbl-productive). These represent the answer to the non-traditional-tissue and productive-infection questions: bona fide, high-confidence productive beta/gamma-HPV infections do occur in primary skin and skin-associated lesions, but they are the exception against a null background.

### The HPV type landscape is partitioned by population

The HPV-type-by-tier catalogue (@supptbl-types) recapitulates these conclusions in a single descriptive view, and the corrected tiering sharpens it. The high-risk mucosal types HPV16/HPV18 are confined almost entirely to cell-line material (`r ciA("HPV16","cell_line")` and `r ciA("HPV18","cell_line")` of cell-line libraries). Productive controls are dominated by cutaneous wart types (HPV57, HPV2, HPV27) plus the low-risk mucocutaneous HPV6/HPV11 and gamma types (HPV4, HPV-mKN1). The EV tier carries precisely the beta-types the syndrome is defined by (HPV9, HPV14, HPV20, HPV25, HPV47) alongside an alpha co-detection. Peri-lesional mucosa carries the mucosal alpha repertoire of its adjacent condylomata (HPV11 in `r ciA("HPV11","peri_lesional")` of libraries, HPV42, HPV6, HPV74, HPV90). Unselected skin, by contrast, contributes no HPV type at all above the two-library display threshold except two HPV18 contamination calls: its beta/gamma reservoir is real but sits entirely below the assignment threshold, and is recovered only at the detection tier (below). The genuine neoplasia-associated productive infections are the gamma/alpha types noted above (HPV12, HPV16, HPV96, HPV182). Collapsed from type to genus (@suppfig-genus), the same partition is a single picture: productive controls are alpha with a gamma minority, EV biopsies are essentially pure beta (`r kG("Beta","EV")` libraries), peri-lesional mucosa is purely alpha, cell lines are alpha, and unselected skin is flat and low across alpha, beta and gamma, with the study's only nu detections. Cutaneous neoplasia is the one tissue tier in which beta exceeds alpha (`r ciG("Beta","Neoplasia")` versus `r ciG("Alpha","Neoplasia")`), the genus-level shadow of a beta-HPV footprint. The epidemiological reservoir of cutaneous beta/gamma HPV in healthy skin is therefore real but transcriptionally quiet, productive disease is the property of warts and EV, and HPV-associated cutaneous neoplasia carries the virus, when at all, as a trace, non-productive footprint.

Extending this catalogue below the assignment threshold answers the descriptive question of *which* types make up the trace. A detection-tier re-map of the HPV-positive but untyped libraries, taking the best-hit reference from unique alignments at sub-threshold coverage, resolved a confident low-coverage type for `r stats$trace_resolved` of `r stats$trace_n` such libraries across `r stats$trace_ntypes` types (@supptbl-trace). This recovers the expected commensal signal at the sensitivity floor: healthy skin carried a diverse cutaneous reservoir (`r stats$trace_skin_cut` of `r stats$trace_skin_n` resolved skin calls were beta-, gamma- or nu-types, including HPV12/HPV20, HPV4/HPV65/HPV134 and candidate skin-virome types), cutaneous neoplasia the carcinoma-associated beta and gamma types (HPV5, HPV12, HPV182, HPV222), while the mucosal HPV16/HPV18 signal stayed confined to cell-line material and a low-level contamination overlay. These are low-coverage, non-productive detections that identify the type without bearing on productivity, and so extend the type catalogue rather than qualify the trace-not-productive conclusion.

### A Bayesian re-analysis under weakly-informative priors confirms the contrasts

To confirm these conclusions are not artefacts of the frequentist framework or of the near-complete separation in the strongest contrast, we refitted the positivity, depth-controlled detection and productivity models as Bayesian logistic regressions under weakly-informative priors (Normal(0, 2.5) on the log-odds coefficients; Methods), summarising each effect by its posterior median odds ratio, 95% credible interval (CrI) and posterior probability of direction (@supptbl-bayes). The contamination enrichment and the trace excess were reproduced essentially unchanged and with near-certainty (cell-line OR `r bor(bget("M1_cell_line"))`, engineered OR `r bor(bget("M1_engineered"))`, neoplasia trace OR `r bor(bget("M2a_neoplasia_vs_skin_any"))`; each with P(OR > 1) > 0.999). Crucially, the productive-controls-versus-skin contrast, whose frequentist odds ratio (`r fo(stats$fish_or)`) is inflated and unstable under separation, regularised to a finite but still enormous posterior OR of `r bor(bget("M2c_controls_vs_skin_floor"))` (`r bor(bget("M2c_controls_vs_skin_floor_studentt"))` under a heavier-tailed Student-*t* prior): the productive gap between warts/EV and skin is real, not a separation artefact. Deeper sequencing within neoplasia again bought no productive-level detection (OR `r bor(bget("M2d_depth_within_neoplasia"))`, P(OR > 1) = `r pdir(bget("M2d_depth_within_neoplasia")$p_gt1)`), and the warts/EV-versus-neoplasia productivity contrast held (OR `r bor(bget("M3_controls_vs_neoplasia"))`, P(OR > 1) = `r pdir(bget("M3_controls_vs_neoplasia")$p_gt1)`). The neoplasia-versus-skin comparison at floor level, whose frequentist interval is wide because it rests on `r stats$neo_pos_floor` above-floor libraries, shrinks under the prior but stays clearly positive (OR `r bor(bget("M2b_neoplasia_vs_skin_floor"))`, P(OR > 1) = `r pdir(bget("M2b_neoplasia_vs_skin_floor")$p_gt1)`): the small floor-level elevation of neoplasia over clean skin is genuine. It is nonetheless negligible beside the near-four-orders-of-magnitude productive-control effect, and it does not alter the trace-not-productive conclusion.
